messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "we're trying to make a small rehearsal recording archive easier to search. can you look over these details and suggest practical ways to improve findability, not the sound quality? there are 42 recordings from the Harborlight Players' 2018 spring season, all made on a handheld recorder. the files are named with the date and the word rehearsal, but some dates use YYYY-MM-DD and others use month-name-day. the folder has three productions: The Glass Orchard, Northbound, and Late Train. Only the production title appears in the folder names, not in the file names. The archive has a spreadsheet with recording date, room, and production, though two room cells are blank. Nobody has checked whether the spreadsheet dates match the file names yet, and we don't know if every recording has a complete cast list. please base suggestions on those details and don't assume the missing checks have been done. i'd like a short response that first points to the evidence in what i gave you and then gives recommendations, so the recommendations don't come before their evidence. that's specifically about recommendations; you can use headings if useful. we need ideas we could use while organizing the existing files, not a proposal for buying a new archive system.", "output": "Review the details below and suggest practical ways to improve the findability of the existing rehearsal recording archive, not its sound quality. Base your suggestions only on the information provided, and do not assume that unchecked details have been verified.

The archive contains 42 recordings from the Harborlight Players' 2018 spring season, all made on a handheld recorder. The files are named with the date and the word “rehearsal,” but dates use both YYYY-MM-DD and month-name-day formats. The folder has three productions: The Glass Orchard, Northbound, and Late Train. Production titles appear in folder names, not file names. A spreadsheet lists each recording's date, room, and production; two room cells are blank. No one has checked whether spreadsheet dates match the file names, and it is unknown whether every recording has a complete cast list.

Keep the response short. For each recommendation, present the supporting evidence from these details first. Headings are optional. Focus on ideas for organizing the existing files; do not propose buying a new archive system."}]
